description: Ruthenium is a rare transition metal belonging to the platinum group of the periodic table with symbol Ru and atomic number 44. It is a polyvalent hard white metal that is unreactive to most chemicals. The element was discovered in 1844 by Karl Ernst Claus at Kazan State University and named in honor of Russia.
uses: Most ruthenium produced is used in wear-resistant electrical contacts and thick-film resistors. It is also used in platinum alloys, as a chemical catalyst, and as a capping layer for extreme ultraviolet photomasks in semiconductor lithography. Ruthenium tetroxide is used as an intermediate in the purification of ruthenium from ores and radiowastes.
characteristics: Ruthenium is a hard white metal that does not tarnish at ambient conditions but oxidizes upon heating to 800°C. It has four crystal modifications and is not attacked by acids including aqua regia, but is attacked by sodium hypochlorite at room temperature and halogens at high temperatures. Small amounts of ruthenium increase the hardness of platinum and palladium, and it can increase the corrosion resistance of titanium markedly.
